from.place: Affine case: the restriction map from the compactification and its boundary kernel, followed by the degree splitting

title: Restriction of Picard groups across a finite boundary
statement: Let $C$ be a smooth affine connected curve over an algebraically closed field $k$ [def-sc-curves], let $C\hookrightarrow\overline C$ be a smooth proper connected compactification [lem-sc-compactification], and let $S=\overline C\setminus C$. Then restriction of invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module] defines a surjective homomorphism on Picard groups [def-sc-picard-group] $\operatorname{Pic}(\overline C)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ whose kernel is the subgroup generated by the classes $[P]=[\mathcal O_{\overline C}(P)]$ for $P\in S$. After choosing $P_0\in S$ and splitting degree by $[P_0]$, this identifies the induced map $\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)/\langle[P]-[P_0]:P\in S\rangle\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ (with $\operatorname{Pic}^0$ as in [def-sc-pic0]) with an isomorphism.

source.place: Proof: restriction and boundary divisors, followed by the degree splitting

proof.text: Use the divisor-class isomorphism [lem-sc-divisor-class-curve] for the smooth connected curves $C$ and $\overline C$. Restriction of divisors $\operatorname{Div}(\overline C)\to\operatorname{Div}(C)$ forgets the coefficients at the finite set $S$, so it is surjective with kernel $B:=\bigoplus_{P\in S}\mathbf Z[P]$. The curves have the same function field, and the divisor of a rational function restricts to the divisor of the same function; hence principal divisors map onto principal divisors. If a divisor on $\overline C$ restricts to a principal divisor $\operatorname{div}_C(f)$, subtracting $\operatorname{div}_{\overline C}(f)$ leaves a divisor in $B$. This divisor-class map is the restriction of invertible modules: for a divisor $D$ on $\overline C$ one has $\mathcal O_{\overline C}(D)|_C=\mathcal O_C(D|_C)$, since both are the subsheaf of the constant sheaf of the common function field cut out by the same local conditions at the points of $C$. Thus restriction descends to a surjective homomorphism $r:\operatorname{Pic}(\overline C)\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)$, and its kernel is exactly the subgroup generated by the classes $[P]=[\mathcal O_{\overline C}(P)]$ for $P\in S$; equivalently, $\operatorname{Pic}(\overline C)/B\cong\operatorname{Pic}(C)$.

source.place: Proof: first paragraph, restriction and boundary divisors

proof.text: Choose $P_0\in S$. By [lem-sc-pic-proper-decomposition], the degree map on $\operatorname{Pic}(\overline C)$ has kernel $\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)$, and [def-sc-pic0] gives $\deg[P_0]=1$. Define $q(x)=x-\deg(x)[P_0]$. Then $q$ is a homomorphism onto $\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)$ and is the identity there, with kernel $\mathbf Z[P_0]$. If $B$ is the subgroup generated by the boundary classes, then $B=\mathbf Z[P_0]+\Lambda$, where $\Lambda=\langle[P]-[P_0]:P\in S\rangle\subseteq\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)$, and $q(B)=\Lambda$. Thus $q$ induces an isomorphism $\operatorname{Pic}(\overline C)/B\cong\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)/\Lambda$.

source.place: Proof: first paragraph, splitting by P0

proof.text: Combining the quotient isomorphism $\operatorname{Pic}(\overline C)/B\cong\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ from step 1 with the isomorphism $\operatorname{Pic}(\overline C)/B\cong\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)/\Lambda$ from step 2 identifies the induced map $\operatorname{Pic}^0(\overline C)/\Lambda\to\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ with an isomorphism. The original restriction map is therefore surjective, has the stated boundary-generated kernel, and has the asserted degree-splitting description.

lean.statement: theorem Scheme.Hom.pic_restriction_boundary {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f] [IsAffine C] (c : Compactification f) [IsConnectedCurve c.g] [hsm : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 c.g] : Function.Surjective (Scheme.Pic.mapHom c.i) ∧ (Scheme.Pic.mapHom c.i).ker = Subgroup.closure {L | ∃ P : closedPoints c.Z, P.val ∉ Set.range c.i.base ∧ L = @Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint k _ c.Z ⟨c.g⟩ hsm P} ∧ ∀ (P₀ : closedPoints c.Z), P₀.val ∉ Set.range c.i.base → ∃ (G : Subgroup c.Z.Pic) (_ : (G : Set c.Z.Pic) = c.g.picZero) (Λ : Subgroup G), Subgroup.map G.subtype Λ = Subgroup.closure {L | ∃ P : closedPoints c.Z, P.val ∉ Set.range c.i.base ∧ L = @Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint k _ c.Z ⟨c.g⟩ hsm P / @Scheme.Pic.ofClosedPoint k _ c.Z ⟨c.g⟩ hsm P₀} ∧ ∃ e : (G ⧸ Λ) ≃* C.Pic, ∀ L : G, e (QuotientGroup.mk L) = Scheme.Pic.mapHom c.i L.val
